summary.headline: Mamata Machinery FY26 revenue fell about 8% to Rs 233.1 crore and EBITDA margin dropped to 8.2%, which management attributes mainly to a 50% US decline and one-offs.
summary.overview: FY26 was a consolidation year: revenue from operations fell about 8% to Rs 233.1 crore (FY25: Rs 254.6 crore) and Q4 revenue was Rs 73.9 crore versus Rs 111 crore a year earlier. The US business (including Canada and Mexico) fell close to 50%, hit by unresolved tariffs through Q2-Q3, then West Asia uncertainty and higher polymer prices in Q4. EBITDA fell to Rs 19.1 crore (8.2% margin) from Rs 54.6 crore (21.4%), and PAT to Rs 15.1 crore from Rs 40.8 crore. Management says the company remains debt-free with Rs 69.26 crore cash and guides FY27 revenue growth of about 15% with margin normalisation toward about 20%.

segments.name: Converting machinery
segments.commentary: US converting sales fell from Rs 31.63 crore to Rs 5.93 crore (-81%). Domestic converting grew over 6% and rest-of-world converting grew 23%, but the segment moderated overall because of the US share.

segments.name: Packaging machinery
segments.commentary: Packaging revenue was flat to down about 1%, at roughly Rs 48-49 crore. US packaging fell from Rs 36.8 crore to Rs 29.4 crore, while domestic packaging grew about 55%.

segments.name: Co-extrusion
segments.commentary: Marginal degrowth due to lumpy order timing. Three large nine-layer orders: two executed in FY26, one (about Rs 9 crore) due in H2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at conservatively about 15% over FY26, with management avoiding a truncated base.
EBITDA margin expected to normalise to historical average of about 20% as the top line recovers and one-offs roll off.
US business expected to recover in FY27, with residual headwinds from West Asia affecting capex sentiment.
Domestic packaging growth targeted at 30-40% in FY27 based on the current FMCG pipeline; domestic converting targeted at double-digit growth.
RecTech recyclable film expected to take 12-18 months before meaningful traction; treated as incremental, not part of the 30-40% packaging target.
Europe: incremental revenue of US$2-3 million over the next three to five years; South-East Asia initial business target close to US$1 million.
risks_watch: US recovery depends on tariff stability and West Asia-driven customer capex sentiment; the Rs 3.5 crore Saudi shipment is stalled.
Gross margin fell 6.2 percentage points on mix, lower exports and commodity inflation; watch H1 FY27 gross margin and pass-through.
RecTech adoption timeline of 12-18 months is long and depends on early-adopter FMCG trials and certifications (Europe and US pending).
Europe ramp is slow and depends on the Carpentier GmbH partnership, which is non-exclusive for initial years.
Lumpy co-extrusion and exhibition-linked spends can swing quarterly results.
Order book conversion: Rs 80 crore due in H1 FY27 must be executed on time to support the 15% growth guidance.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term direction and the packaging pipeline, but candid that FY26 was weak. Management attributes the decline to external events (US tariffs, West Asia) and one-offs. Answers on RecTech and Europe were measured and conservative, and some figures (such as the margin split) were deferred or not quantified.
key_quotes: This was a year of consolidation for the company.
We expect profitability to normalize to historical averages of around 20% as the top line recovers and these one-off costs roll off.
It is definitely not because we are cheaper. In fact, we are the most expensive in India today.
We have zero B2C in business. Our entire business is B2B.

vs Rs 111 crore in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.metric: One-time employee cost provision (new wage code)
financial_highlights.value: about Rs 3.05 crore, booked in Q4

financial_highlights.change: about +34% vs Rs 66.64 crore in FY25

qa_highlights.question: Does the FSA exemption and three-year carry-forward mean packaging users face minimal near-term compliance pressure, making FY27-28 the inflection point?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RecTech needs first two or three early adopters after 6-9 month trials, with 12-18 months before traction. RecTech is incremental growth; the 30-40% domestic packaging target is based on the current FMCG pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Are there other markets to diversify into if the US stays weak? What is the Russia revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Packaging is being taken to Africa and Europe in FY27; a Russia branch office was approved. Russia has no packaging revenue yet, only a couple of converting machines. Converting is already present in about 84 countries.

qa_highlights.question: Order book split and margin difference between exports and domestic?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book Rs 89.59 crore: 62% exports, 38% domestic. Gross margin about 60% on exports vs about 42-43% domestically. Rs 80 crore executes in H1 FY27 and Rs 9 crore in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Were any orders delayed due to West Asia, and what is the FY27 growth expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Three machines worth about Rs 3.5 crore for Saudi Arabia are ready but unshipped. Management said it will not use a truncated base and conservatively expects FY27 revenue about 15% above FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins normalise, and who bears the input cost increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins to normalise as top line recovers and one-offs (exhibition spend, wage code) roll off; costs are semi-variable. Majority of cost increase passed on to customers project-by-project; no numeric split given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the US decline is in the US entity versus Canada and Mexico, and how were packaging and converting US figures split?
qa_highlights.answer: The 50% drop includes the US, Canada and Mexico. US packaging fell from Rs 36.8 crore to Rs 29.4 crore; US converting fell from Rs 31.63 crore to Rs 5.93 crore (-81%).

qa_highlights.question: What is the Europe market size and the Carpentier partnership's scope?
qa_highlights.answer: Addressable market about US$800 million for the product lines; target US$2-3 million incremental over 3-5 years. Partnership with Carpentier GmbH is non-exclusive for Western Europe in initial years; Eastern Europe to use additional channel partners.

capex_capacity: Q4 FY26 order flow: capex decisions by customers were put on hold in Q4 amid West Asia conflict and polymer price spike; a few US orders came in during Q4 and are expected to execute over the next two months.
Multi-machine VFFS order from a leading Indian snacks and namkeen brand: 4 machines delivered in FY26 (3 in India), orders for 18 more scheduled for delivery in H1 FY27.
First packaging machine order from South Africa, scheduled for delivery in Q2 FY27; Africa groundwork reported as 18 months old.
Order book at FY26 end Rs 89.59 crore (62% exports, 38% domestic): Rs 80 crore due in H1 FY27, Rs 9 crore nine-layer co-extrusion line due in H2 FY27.
Three machines (about Rs 3.5 crore) ready on shop floor for Saudi Arabia shipment, stalled since late Feb/early Mar 2026 due to Middle East crisis.
Co-extrusion: two of three large nine-layer orders executed in FY26; one to be executed in H2 FY27.
demand_pricing: US business (incl. Canada and Mexico) fell close to 50%, or about Rs 31 crore gross; US converting fell from Rs 31.63 crore to Rs 5.93 crore (-81%), US packaging from Rs 36.8 crore to Rs 29.4 crore (about -20%).
Recovery in FY26 gap of Rs 31 crore: domestic converting +Rs 3 crore (about 6%), domestic packaging +Rs 6 crore, rest-of-world converting +Rs 11.5 crore; total Rs 20.65 crore recovered.
Domestic packaging grew about 55% in FY26; domestic converting grew over 6%; rest-of-world converting grew 23%.

Gross margin 54.6% vs 60.8%; management cited lower export share (exports higher margin, about 60% gross margin vs about 42-43% domestic on order book), adverse mix (lower co-extrusion), and H2 commodity inflation; 6.2 pp EBITDA margin impact.

Pricing: most of the polymer/input cost increase passed on to customers on project-by-project basis; management said it was the most expensive machine supplier in India and won on cost-to-output ratio, not price.
Competition: converting is highly fragmented (customers in about 84-86 countries per management); packaging customers are FMCG/organised-sector MNCs and marquee brands.

Europe: addressable market for product lines about US$800 million; initial target US$2-3 million incremental revenue over 3-5 years via Carpentier GmbH (non-exclusive for Western Europe in initial years).

RecTech: trials of 6-9 months with large FMCG companies; needs 2-3 early adopters; 12-18 months before traction; certifications (Indian Institute of Packaging, CPET) done, EU/US Class A testing pending.
Russia: no revenue yet; only a couple of converting machines shipped; branch office approved for CIS.
